docs.title: Acceptance profiles
docs.text: How far speculative decoding advances a request per verification step. The registry holds measured acceptance lengths with their provenance; a workload, a scenario or the command line may state their own; and a run resolves exactly one of them and records where it came from.

docs.title: The quantity
docs.text:
The canonical value is the mean acceptance length (AL): the tokens a request gains per verification step, counting the target's bonus token. For K speculative tokens it lies in [1, K + 1]. It is what InferenceX's golden curves publish and what the engines take (vLLM synthetic_acceptance_length, SGLang SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN).

Two other quantities are derived from it, and each has one name here:

  • The acceptance rate is the accepted fraction of drafts, (AL − 1) / K. It is vLLM's logged "Avg Draft acceptance rate" and inference-sim's --speculative-acceptance-rate. The two agree only when every step drafts all K: with a drafter that verifies fewer on some steps, such as DSpark under enable_adaptive_verification, vLLM's logged rate (accepted over drafted tokens, vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py:107-110) divides by the drafts actually proposed and diverges from (AL − 1) / K. The per-token probability p of the speculative-decoding papers is a different quantity and is never called a rate in this schema.
  • Per-position rates p1..pK follow vLLM's synthetic_acceptance_rates: pi is the unconditional probability that the first i drafts are all accepted. They are non-increasing, each lies in [0, 1], and they sum to AL − 1.

No source in scope publishes per-position rates, so they are optional everywhere. A consumer that needs a distribution derives one with MinimumVarianceRates, which is vLLM v0.31.0's _acceptance_length_to_rates (vllm/config/speculative.py:557-564):

rates = [1.0] * floor(AL - 1) + [frac(AL - 1)] + [0.0] * rest, truncated to K

This is how vLLM, and the InferenceX runs that force a published AL, realise one, so a simulator using it reproduces those runs. Natural acceptance spreads more than this schedule does, so per-request tails derived from it are optimistic.

Acceptance is not the kernel's input. K and the method stay in the deployment's speculative block, because they change what a step costs; acceptance changes only how far requests advance.

docs.title: Profile set
docs.text:
A registry file under acceptance/, named by its file. This one carries real values from InferenceX's golden SPEED-Bench curves:

kind: AcceptanceProfileSet
name: inferencex-golden-al
caveats:
  - Coding only. Every curve is SPEED-Bench Qualitative coding; other categories have none.
  - Measured on B300. Reuse on another part is recorded by the resolver.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark at K 6-8 was refused by the image, so it has no value.
profiles:
  - model: deepseek-v4.1-flash
    speculative_method: dspark
    num_spec_tokens: 5
    thinking: "off"
    category: coding
    acceptance_length: 4.07
    method: measured
    provenance: &dsv41
      source: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/dsv41flash_dspark.yaml
      run: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34493175056
      benchmark: SPEED-Bench Qualitative
      prompts: 80
      hardware: b300
      engine_image: vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909
      tp: 4
      sampling: {temperature: 1.0, max_tokens: 4096}
      settings:
        draft_sample_method: probabilistic
        rejection_sample_method: block
  - model: deepseek-v4.1-flash
    speculative_method: dspark
    num_spec_tokens: 5
    thinking: "on"
    category: coding
    acceptance_length: 3.51
    method: measured
    provenance: *dsv41
  - model: glm-5.3
    speculative_method: mtp
    num_spec_tokens: 3
    thinking: "on"
    category: coding
    acceptance_length: 2.99
    method: copied
    copied_from: glm-5.2-fp8/mtp/k3/thinking-on/coding
    rationale: >
      Provisional. GLM-5.3 shares GLM-5.2's base and layer topology, so GLM-5.2's curve is
      the closest measured reference; replace it with a run on GLM-5.3.
    provenance:
      source: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/glm5.3_mtp.yaml
      run: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/28058352479
      hardware: b300
      sampling: {temperature: 1.0, top_p: 0.95, max_tokens: 4096}
Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always AcceptanceProfileSet. name string yes The set's identity. By convention it equals the file name, which is what a scenario's acceptance.profiles uses. caveats list of strings no What the set does not cover and how far its values travel. No entry may be empty. profiles list yes At least one profile, below.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A profile is keyed by model, speculative method, K, thinking mode and workload category. Two profiles with one key are an error.

Key Type Required Meaning model string yes The catalog model name, not the source's spelling of it. speculative_method string yes The engine's method name, as a deployment's engine.speculative.method states it. num_spec_tokens integer yes K. At least 1. thinking string yes on or off. One of the thinking modes. category string yes The workload category, such as coding. Lower-case letters, digits, _ and -. acceptance_length number yes AL, in [1, K + 1]. per_position_rates list of numbers no K rates, each in [0, 1], non-increasing, summing to AL − 1 within 0.01. method string yes How the value was obtained. One of the methods except not_charged. provenance mapping unless method is assumed Where it was measured, below. rationale string unless method is measured The reasoning behind a value that was not measured. copied_from string with method copied The profile it was copied from, as model/method/k<K>/thinking-<mode>/category.

docs.title: provenance
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning source string yes The document the value was read from. run string no The job that measured it, such as a GitHub Actions run. benchmark string no The prompt set, such as SPEED-Bench Qualitative. prompts integer no How many prompts it covered. Not negative. hardware string with method measured The catalog chip it was measured on. A resolution on other hardware records this. engine_image string with method measured The engine image or release that ran. tp integer no The tensor-parallel width it ran at. Not negative. sampling mapping with method measured The decoding configuration, below. settings mapping no Other engine settings that bear on acceptance, by name, such as rejection_sample_method.

docs.title: provenance.sampling
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning temperature number yes Not negative. 0 is greedy decoding. top_p number no In (0, 1]. top_k integer no At least −1; −1 and 0 disable it. max_tokens integer no Output cap. Not negative.

docs.title: Inline values
docs.text:
A workload's acceptance, a scenario's acceptance.value, and the value a command line supplies all take this form. A value names the K it was stated for; at a deployment that speculates another K it is refused rather than rescaled.

Key Type Required Meaning num_spec_tokens integer yes The K the value was stated for. At least 1. acceptance_length number one of three AL, in [1, K + 1]. acceptance_rate number one of three (AL − 1) / K, in [0, 1]. Not with acceptance_length. per_position_rates list of numbers one of three K rates, as for a profile. Alone, they state AL as 1 + their sum; with either of the others, they must agree with it. source string no Where the value came from, recorded with the resolution.

docs.title: Scenario pin
docs.text:
The value of a scenario's acceptance key.

acceptance:
  value:
    num_spec_tokens: 3
    acceptance_length: 2.8
    source: synthetic_acceptance_length in the scored run's server log

To use another profile set for the run, and to accept coding's curve for traffic that has none of its own:

acceptance:
  profiles: inferencex-golden-al
  fallback_category: coding
Key Type Required Meaning profiles string no An acceptance-profile set under acceptance/ in the registry, consulted in place of the default. Not with value. value mapping no An inline value, above. fallback_category string no The category to use when the workload's has no curve. The substitution is recorded. Not with value.

A pin must set at least one key.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
acceptance.Resolve takes the run's model, method and K, the registry sets, the workload's terms, the scenario's pin and the command line's value, and returns the acceptance length, the per-position rates, and which layer supplied them. The highest layer that states acceptance wins; layers are not merged.

Layer Supplies acceptance by registry the profile matching (model, method, K, the workload's thinking mode and category) in the registry sets, the default workload the workload's own acceptance value scenario the pin's value, or the matching profile in the set its profiles names cli the command line's value, such as --speculative-acceptance-rate at the deployment's K

registry · workload · scenario · cli

Nothing falls back silently. A lookup is refused when

  • the workload states no thinking mode, or no category and no fallback was requested;
  • no profile matches and no fallback_category was requested, or the fallback has no profile either;
  • two registry sets both match;
  • the scenario names a set that was not supplied. The registry is not consulted in its place.

A value stated for a K other than the deployment's is refused at every layer. The resolution records the profile set and entry, the cited source, the category a fallback replaced, the hardware a profile was measured on when it differs from the run's, and whether the rates were derived.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A profile set is invalid if

  • kind is not AcceptanceProfileSet, name is empty, there are no profiles, or a caveat is empty;
  • two profiles share a key;
  • a profile has no model or speculative_method, thinking is not on or off, or category is malformed;
  • num_spec_tokens is less than 1, or acceptance_length is not finite or lies outside [1, K + 1];
  • per_position_rates has other than K entries, an entry outside [0, 1], rises, or sums more than 0.01 from AL − 1;
  • method is not recognized or is not_charged, or a field the method requires, per the table above, is missing;
  • a provenance has no source, a negative count, an empty setting, or sampling with no temperature, a negative one, a top_p outside (0, 1] or a top_k below −1.

An inline value is invalid if num_spec_tokens is less than 1, it states no acceptance, it states both acceptance_length and acceptance_rate, either lies outside its range, or its rates are invalid or disagree with it. A pin is invalid if it sets nothing, sets both profiles and value, sets fallback_category with value, or its value is invalid.

With a deployment in the bundle, every inline value (the scenario's pin, its trace's, its replay's, merged with its catalog entry when the bundle carries one, a catalog replay's, and the workload shape's) must name the K of each pool that speculates. When no pool speculates, a stated value draws a warning.

Source: spec/acceptance.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
One command for each data repository, and one for measured runs before they are committed. Each validates every document under the path it is given and exits with a code a CI step can read.

go run github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/cmd/validate-catalog@<version>      <catalog root>
go run github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/cmd/validate-registry@<version>     <registry root>
go run github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/cmd/validate-measurements@<version> [-local] <measurements dir>

Both write every problem to standard error. validate-catalog writes to standard output a heading for each kind of file and one line for each artifact that validates: each file, or each storage class in devices/storage.yaml. validate-registry writes one line per set to standard output, FAILED for a set that does not validate. Each ends with a summary line: all N ... validate on standard output, or N of M ... failed on standard error. Warnings are printed and do not fail the run. Both run the field layer only: these documents name no engine version, so no rules pack applies.

docs.title: validate-catalog
docs.text:
Path Validated as models/*/graph.yaml a model graph, whose name must equal the directory. A model directory without one is skipped. models/*/config.json required in every model directory; must be a non-empty JSON object. models/*/model.yaml required in every model directory; a model identity, whose name must equal the directory. hardware/*.yaml a chip networks/*.yaml a fabric devices/storage.yaml storage classes. Optional. workloads/*.yaml a workload shape, or a replay workload when its top-level key is replay: measurements/ as validate-measurements does, without -local. Optional.

Only files ending in .yaml are read in the flat directories. A path is treated as a catalog if it contains at least one of models/, hardware/, networks/, workloads/, devices/ and measurements/.

docs.title: validate-registry
docs.text:
Every file under coefficients/ whose extension is .yaml or .yml, in any letter case and at any depth, is validated as a coefficient set. Symbolic links to directories are not followed. A scenario can refer only to a set at the top level of coefficients/ with a .yaml extension, by its file name; a set elsewhere validates but cannot be named.

Files under acceptance/, found the same way, are validated as acceptance-profile sets, each reported as acceptance/<file>. The directory is optional.

docs.title: validate-measurements
docs.text:
sources.yaml is validated as the licence registry, and every <license_ref>/*.yaml as a measured run against it. A run's name must equal its file name, its license_ref its directory, and its stated verdict the computed one. duplicate_of and supersedes must name another run in the directory. A YAML file at the top level other than sources.yaml fails. Without -local, every run's licence must permit redistribute; with it, scoring alone suffices, for output that stays out of the repository.

It writes one line per file to standard output, the verdict for a run, and exits 0 when every file validates, 1 when any fails, and 2 on wrong arguments or a path that is not a directory.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code validate-catalog validate-registry 0 every artifact validated every set validated 1 an artifact failed to load or validate a coefficient or acceptance set failed to load or validate 2 wrong arguments; the root does not exist; none of the six directories is present; or nothing was found to validate wrong arguments; the root does not exist; coefficients/ could not be read; or it holds no coefficient sets

Source: cmd/validate-catalog, cmd/validate-registry, cmd/validate-measurements.

docs.title: Coefficient set
docs.text:
A set of coefficients for a cost model. Each entry records its value and unit, how it was obtained, the evidence for it, and the hardware and layouts over which it holds. The registry owns the sets; every consumer loads them through this schema.

The set below is illustrative; its values are not real coefficients. The registry's sets are in coefficients/.

kind: CoefficientSet
name: example-set
coefficients:
  - gemm_eps_max_bf16:
      value: 0.78
      units: dimensionless
      method: measured
      fitted: true
      ci95: [0.74, 0.81]
      scope: {hardware: [h100]}
  - gemm_eps_max_bf16:
      value: 0.81
      units: dimensionless
      method: measured
      fitted: true
      scope: {hardware: [h200]}
  - mfu_prefill:
      value: 0.32
      units: dimensionless
      method: literature
      fitted: false
      sources:
        - {kind: discussion, cite: "inference-sim#589", role: primary}
      rationale: >
        L40S prefill MFU discount; see the cited discussion.
      scope: {hardware: [l40s]}
  - pd_transfer_base_latency:
      value: 50
      units: us_per_transfer
      method: assumed
      fitted: false
      rationale: >
        A placeholder until a measurement exists.
      scope: {hardware: [h100, h200]}

Each entry in coefficients is a map with a single key, the entry's name. A name key inside an entry is accepted and replaced by that map key. A set is complete in itself: it does not inherit from another set. A scenario may still name several sets, and how a cost model combines them is described under Selecting an entry.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always CoefficientSet. name string yes The set's identity. By convention, not checked, it equals the file name, which is what a scenario's coefficients uses. coefficients list yes At least one entry, each - <entry name>: {...}.

docs.title: Entries
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning value number unless method is not_charged The coefficient. Zero exactly when method is not_charged. units string yes One of the units. method string yes How the value was obtained. One of the methods. fitted boolean yes Whether the value comes from fitting a curve. Must be present even when false. scope mapping yes Where the value holds, below. At least one dimension. ci95 [low, high] no 95% confidence interval. Must contain value. sources list depends on method Citations, below. If present, not empty. rationale string depends on method The reasoning behind a value that was not measured. copied_from string with method copied The scope the value was copied from. supersedes string no An entry this one replaces. validated string or list no Names of metrics the value has been checked against, such as itl. Free text. unsupported string or list no Names of metrics it has been found not to hold for. Free text.

docs.title: scope
docs.text:
Each dimension lists the values the coefficient holds for. An empty scope is not "everywhere"; it means the range is unknown, and it is rejected.

Key Type Required Meaning hardware list of strings no Chips. model list of strings no Models. tp list of integers no Tensor-parallel widths. ep list of integers no Expert-parallel widths. nodes_spanned list of integers no How many nodes a collective crosses.

Dtype and backend are not scope dimensions. Both are part of the entry's name, as in gemm_eps_max_bf16.

docs.title: sources
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes One of the source kinds. cite string yes The reference: an issue, a paper, a datasheet URL. role string yes One of the source roles.

docs.title: Identity is name and scope
docs.text: Two entries may share a name if their scopes differ. The set above has two gemm_eps_max_bf16 entries, one for H100 and one for H200. Two entries with the same name and the same scope are an error, because a cost model would use whichever came last. Scopes are compared without regard to order: [h100, h200] and [h200, h100] are the same scope.

docs.title: Selecting an entry
docs.text: The schema defines what an entry says. Choosing among entries is the cost model's job, and blis-latency-kernel does it as follows. An entry applies to a deployment if, for every dimension its scope states, the list includes the deployment's value; hardware and model names are compared without regard to case, and a dimension the scope omits does not constrain it. The kernel reads the scenario's sets in order and, within each set, its entries in order, and the last applicable entry for each name is the one it uses. A later set can therefore override part of an earlier one. Entries that do not apply are skipped. Construction fails if no entry applies at all, or if the cost model needs a coefficient no applicable entry supplies.

docs.title: What a method requires
docs.text: Method rationale sources Other measured — — Allows fitted: true. A source is expected but not required. calibrated required at least one of kind measured_case Allows fitted: true. validated must name the held-out metrics. literature required at least one vendor_spec required at least one copied required — copied_from required. assumed required — not_charged required — value must be 0.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A set fails to load if an entry is not a single-key map, an entry has no fitted key, sources is present but empty, ci95 is not a two-element list, validated or unsupported is neither a string nor a list of strings, or any mapping has a key its type does not declare.

A loaded set is invalid if

  • kind is not CoefficientSet, name is empty, or there are no entries;
  • an entry has no name, or repeats another entry's name and scope;
  • value is not finite, units or method is not recognized, or scope is empty;
  • value is 0 with a method other than not_charged, or nonzero with not_charged;
  • fitted is true with a method other than measured or calibrated;
  • a companion field the method requires, per the table above, is missing;
  • a source has an unrecognized kind or role, or an empty cite;
  • ci95 has a non-finite end, has low above high, or does not contain value.

Source: spec/coefficient.

docs.title: Connector registry
docs.text:
Which KV-connector names a deployment may use, which engine interface each implements, and which engine model reproduces its behaviour. A deployment's `offload.connector` and `pd_transfer.connector` are looked up here rather than in a list compiled into a simulator, so a connector that behaves like an existing one is data, not code.

# A KV-connector registry. The built-in entries for vLLM live in blis-vllm; this example
# shows the shape with two of them.
kind: ConnectorRegistry
name: example
connectors:
  OffloadingConnector:
    upstream: KVConnectorBase_V1
    behaves_like: offloading
    roles: [offload]
    evidence: diff-test @ vLLM v0.32.0
  NixlConnector:
    upstream: KVConnectorBase_V1
    behaves_like: nixl-pull
    roles: [pd_transfer]
    evidence: diff-test @ vLLM v0.32.0

An entry earns behaves_like only by evidence. Implementing an engine's connector interface is not the same as behaving like one of its connectors, so a vendor connector is registered only once it passes the differential tests the engine module runs against the engine release; until then it is unsupported. This page describes the shape. The entries for vLLM live with the engine model, in blis-vllm.

Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always ConnectorRegistry. name string yes The registry's identity. connectors mapping yes At least one entry, by connector name exactly as the engine registers it (vLLM's KVConnectorFactory.register_connector). Key Type Required Meaning upstream string yes The engine interface the connector implements, as the engine names it. Which interfaces exist is the engine module's to check. behaves_like string yes The engine model that reproduces the connector's behaviour, in the engine module that owns the registry. roles list yes What a deployment may use it for: offload, pd_transfer, composite. Each at most once. evidence string yes How the entry earned behaves_like, such as diff-test @ vLLM v0.32.0.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A registry is invalid if kind is not ConnectorRegistry, name is empty, it has no connectors, a connector name is blank or has surrounding spaces (names match the engine's exactly), or an entry omits upstream, behaves_like or evidence, has no roles, or lists an unknown or repeated role.

Source: spec/connector.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The choices made against a scenario: how its cluster is divided into pools, each pool's parallel layout and engine settings, the KV offload tiers, and how KV moves from prefill to decode. A deployment is validated with its scenario, because most of what makes a layout feasible depends on the cluster.

kind: Deployment
name: 1p3d-ep8
pools:
  - role: prefill
    nodes: 1
    parallel:
      tp: 1
      pp: 1
      dp: 8
      dp_local: 8
      enable_expert_parallel: true
    engine:
      all2all_backend: deepep_high_throughput
      max_num_batched_tokens: 16384
  - role: decode
    nodes: 3
    parallel:
      tp: 1
      pp: 1
      dp: 8
      dp_local: 8
      enable_expert_parallel: true
    engine:
      all2all_backend: deepep_low_latency
      max_num_seqs: 512
offload:
  tiers:
    - tier: cpu_dram
      bytes: 549755813888
pd_transfer:
  connector: NixlConnector

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always Deployment. name string yes The deployment's identity. pools list yes At least one pool, below. offload mapping no KV offload tiers below HBM. pd_transfer mapping if any pool is prefill How KV moves from prefill to decode. router mapping no The inputs of the llm-d router that routes the deployment's requests. Absent: the router's built-in configuration over every pod.

docs.title: Pools
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning role string yes colocated, prefill or decode. nodes integer yes Nodes in the pool, at least 1. parallel mapping yes The parallel layout of each engine in the pool. engine mapping no The engine's settings for the pool, held unopened; the engine model opens and checks it. See below. labels mapping no Kubernetes labels on the pool's model-server pods, as its pod template sets them. The router selects and filters endpoints by them. llm-d.ai/role is derived from role (colocated -> prefill-decode, prefill -> prefill, decode -> decode); given here, it must have that value.

A pool may run several engines with the same layout and settings. Its nodes is the pool's whole extent; one engine may occupy only part of it.

Pools of role prefill and decode come together or not at all, and neither may appear beside a colocated pool.

docs.title: parallel
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning tp integer yes Tensor-parallel width, at least 1. pp integer yes Pipeline-parallel width, at least 1. dp integer yes Data-parallel width, at least 1. dp_local integer no Data-parallel replicas resident on one node. Must divide gpus_per_node and not exceed dp. Zero means the launch decides. data_parallel_load_balancing string no How the data-parallel ranks are exposed, which decides what a router chooses between. One of the load-balancing modes. Omitted, internal. hybrid and external need dp > 1. The rules pack refuses external on a model without experts and hybrid without dp_local, and names the mode that runs when the engine resolves hybrid to another. --api-server-count is not part of it: it sets how many frontend processes share an endpoint, not which ranks a router can reach. pcp integer no Prefill-context-parallel width. Zero or 1 means off. dcp integer no Decode-context-parallel width. Reuses the tensor-parallel ranks; see below. Zero or 1 means off. enable_expert_parallel boolean no Shard MoE experts across ranks. Default false.

There is no key for the expert-parallel width. It is derived: tp × pcp × dp when expert parallelism is enabled, and 1 otherwise. A key for it would let a document state a width no engine would build. Parallel layouts explains this and the checks below in more depth.

docs.title: engine
docs.text: A pool's engine block is the engine's own settings, and this schema holds it unopened: it loads the block as written and passes it through unchanged. The engine model that a scenario's engine_version selects opens it, and its rules check it. A validator passes those rules in (Bundle.Rules), and they report a problem in the block at its path below deployment.pools[i].engine. For vLLM the keys, their defaults and their checks are blis-vllm's (rules/engineconfig, with its reference in blis-vllm's docs/engine-config.md).

docs.title: Offload
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning tiers list yes At least one tier, below. eviction_policy string no KV offload cache policy. Omitted means lru. prefetch_depth integer no How many steps ahead a fetch is issued. connector string no The KV connector that implements offload. spec string no The offloading spec, such as CPUOffloadingSpec. connector_options mapping no The connector's own options, held unopened for the engine model; see below.

docs.title: offload.connector_options
docs.text: The offload connector's own options. This schema holds them unopened, as it does a pool's engine block, and the engine model's rules check them (Bundle.Rules). A problem in them is reported at its path below deployment.offload.connector_options.

docs.title: offload.tiers
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning tier string yes The storage class this tier uses. If the scenario's cluster lists storage, it must be one of those. bytes integer yes Capacity of the tier in bytes, at least 1.

docs.title: PD transfer
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning connector string no The KV connector that moves KV from prefill to decode.

There is no bandwidth key. Transfer bandwidth comes from the scenario's fabric and a registry coefficient, so it cannot be set here.

docs.title: router
docs.text:
Key Type Required Meaning epp_flags list no The router's (EPP's) command-line flags, verbatim, one list entry per flag (--name=value). They select the pool with --pool-name or --endpoint-selector. A Helm chart's epp.flags map is rendered to this list (name: value becomes --name=value). endpoint_picker_config string no The EndpointPickerConfig file, as the router reads it with --config-file; a blank path is an error. Naming the configuration here and in epp_flags is an error. manifests list no Kubernetes manifest files. The router reads their InferencePool, InferenceObjective and InferenceModelRewrite objects; other kinds are ignored. Objectives and rewrites take effect only for an InferencePool (--pool-name); with a standalone pool (--endpoint-selector) the router does not reconcile them, so a consumer may refuse them there.

Paths are relative to the directory of the file that holds the deployment. The block names the router's own inputs and nothing else: scorers, weights, admission and flow control are configured in those files, exactly as for a real deployment, so the same files configure the real router and a simulated one. There is no deployment key for a routing decision. The router here is the Endpoint Picker. The multimodal Coordinator pipeline is a separate llm-d component and is not named by this block; a simulator that cannot host it refuses it at startup.

These checks are syntactic. A deployment that passes them is well formed, not necessarily routable by a given consumer: a simulator refuses, at its startup and with the reason, router flags, plugins or manifests it cannot run faithfully.

pools[].labels are a different kind of input from the three above. In a real deployment the labels live in each pool's pod template; a deployment here has no pod spec, so the labels restate them, so that an InferencePool selector or a label filter has the pods' labels to match.

docs.title: On its own
docs.text:
A deployment is invalid if

  • kind is not Deployment, name is empty, or pools is empty;
  • a pool's role is not recognized, or its nodes is less than 1;
  • tp, pp or dp is less than 1, pcp or dcp is negative, dp_local is negative, or dp_local exceeds dp;
  • dcp does not partition the group it reuses. With pcp at most 1, tp must be divisible by dcp. With pcp above 1, dcp must be 1, pcp or tp × pcp;
  • a prefill pool has no decode pool, a decode pool has no prefill pool, or a colocated pool appears beside either;
  • a prefill pool is present and pd_transfer is absent;
  • offload is present with no tiers, a tier is unnamed or named twice, a tier's bytes is below 1, or prefetch_depth is negative;

It draws a warning if expert parallelism is enabled but the derived width is 1. The checks of a pool's engine block are its engine model's.

docs.title: Against its scenario's cluster
docs.text:
These run when the bundle holds both documents. A deployment without its scenario is itself reported, because these checks would otherwise be skipped.

  • The pools' nodes must sum to the cluster's nodes. A deployment lays out the whole cluster.
  • A pool's dp_local, when set, must divide gpus_per_node.
  • An engine needs one GPU per rank, pp × tp × pcp × dp in all, and they must fit in the pool's nodes. Decode-context and expert parallelism add no ranks.
  • With dp_local set, the local replicas must fit on one node in the way the engine places them. The check refuses only layouts that no launch could place. In the rare case that its bounded search cannot decide, it reports a warning that the layout's fit is unverified.
  • Each offload tier must be one of the cluster's storage classes, if the cluster lists any.

Engine-release checks, such as whether a backend name exists or whether prefill-context parallelism may be combined with data parallelism, are in the rules pack.

Source: spec/deployment.

docs.title: Router contract
docs.text:
Package embed is the interface between a simulator that hosts a request router and the router it hosts. The simulator implements Runtime; the router implements Constructor, Router and Flight. The llm-d router fork is the implementation in use, and inference-sim hosts it.

The boundary is ownership. The host owns simulated time, background work and randomness, the endpoints' lifecycle, and what each engine publishes. The router owns every routing decision and the meaning of its configuration. Router configuration (scorers, weights, profiles) never appears in the contract: it travels as the deployment's own bytes in Config, and what the host needs to know about it comes back as facts in Requirements.

A router is a deterministic function of its Config, the Runtime it runs on and the sequence of calls the host makes. It reads time, starts concurrent work, blocks, draws randomness and reaches the network only through the Runtime.

The package uses the standard library only. A test enforces that rule.

docs.title: Host side
docs.text:
Method Does Now() time.Time The current time. NewTimer(d) Timer, NewTicker(d) Ticker Timers and tickers on the runtime clock. Go(fn) Runs fn concurrently. The runtime may run it until it finishes or parks before returning. Every(ctx, name, interval, fn) Calls fn every interval until ctx is done. WithTimeout, WithDeadlineCause The context functions on the runtime clock. Park(ready) Called by a router goroutine before it blocks; it blocks only while ready() is false. Rand(stream) Rand A named random stream. Local(key, init) any State the router would otherwise keep process-wide.

RoundTripper is an optional capability, found by type assertion, for a runtime that serves the router's outbound HTTP (engine metrics, prompt rendering).

docs.title: Router side
docs.text:
Method Does Constructor(ctx, rt, cfg) (Router, error) Builds a router with no endpoints. Neither it nor work it starts calls Rand before it returns, because the host derives the stream scope from the constructed router. If it fails, it has already stopped what it started. A refused plugin type wraps a *RefusalError. Config.Allow(pluginType) (bool, string) The host's plugin policy. A type the router cannot host for a stated reason is refused with that reason; otherwise Allow decides; a type the router has not audited is refused even when Allow permits it. Config.Logger *slog.Logger Receives the router's logs; nil discards them. Config.Check(Requirements, Pool) error The host's own check, which the router calls after parsing the configuration and before it builds any plugin. A failure is returned unwrapped. Requirements() Facts about the configuration, known from the parsed configuration before any plugin exists: metric flags, inert flags, metrics extractors and sources, KV-event indexes, topology labels, whether it disaggregates. Pool() The pool served. Pool.ID() renders it as Kind.group namespace/name. FlowControl() Whether flow control is on, the longest bounded queue-wait budget and the expiry sweep. IdleSkippable() Whether the host may skip background ticks over an idle period. SetEndpoint, RemoveEndpoint The endpoints and their readiness. Route(ctx, req, done) One routing decision. done receives a Flight and a Decision, or a Rejection, exactly once. WantsKVEvents, IngestKVEvents, ClearKVEvents Engines' KV events, in vLLM's vocabulary (BlockStored, BlockRemoved). Stop() Ends every loop and goroutine the router started.

KVIndexInspector is an optional capability, found by type assertion, for a router that can report its KV-event index per endpoint and tier (KVBlocks). It serves conformance and fidelity tests; a host does not depend on it in production.

A Flight is a dispatched request. The host hands it the response headers (ResponseHeaders, which returns the headers after the router's handling) and the body (ResponseBody), then ends it once: with the last body chunk, or with Terminate (client-disconnect, evicted, error). EvictionSignal is closed when the router revokes the request. It is nil when the router never evicts.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
A Request is what a client sends; the router renders its request headers from it, in sorted key order. :method is POST, :path is Path, content-type is application/json, and x-request-id is ID, always. The others are sent only when the field is set:

Field Header Rendering Objective x-llm-d-inference-objective verbatim FairnessID x-llm-d-inference-fairness-id verbatim TTFTSLO x-llm-d-slo-ttft-ms whole milliseconds, rounded up, when positive TTL x-llm-d-inference-ttl time.Duration.String, when positive; a flow-controlled request's queue-wait budget is the shorter of it and the configured one

docs.title: Rejections
docs.text: RejectKind Meaning no-endpoints No endpoint could serve the request. ttl-expired It waited in flow control past its queue-wait budget. saturated Flow control's queues were at capacity. context-cancelled The client gave up while the router held it. admission An admission check refused it. unavailable The router could not serve it and gave no more specific reason. unclassified Any other outcome. A host treats it as a defect, not as load shedding.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text: embed/embedtest checks a Constructor against the contract, as testing/fstest checks an fs.FS. It drives the router through a fixed scenario on a deterministic Runtime that it provides, and it plays the engines. A Suite supplies one router configuration per behaviour: plain routing, flow control that holds requests, KV-event routing, and optionally eviction and an always-unavailable configuration. It also names a plugin type to refuse. A router passes embedtest.Run(t, suite) when every part behaves as this page describes.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Runtime, Router and Flight are implemented in other repositories, so none of them gains a method within a major version. A new capability is a separate interface. Struct types may gain fields in a minor version; their zero value keeps the earlier meaning. A new RejectKind or Termination value is a minor change, and a host maps a kind it does not know as it maps unclassified.

docs.title: Engine interface
docs.text:
engine.Engine is the interface an inference-engine model implements and a discrete-event simulator calls: the counterpart of the kernel interface for scheduling rather than pricing. One value is one engine instance, the state machine behind one server process.

The boundary follows from who owns time. The simulator owns the clock, the event queue and the decision of when to step. The engine owns every scheduling, KV-cache and connector decision, and the metrics those decisions produce. An engine reads no clock and schedules no event: every call carries the simulated instant as a value (engine.Time, microseconds), and where an engine rule makes work wait until a later instant, the engine reports that instant through NextWake.

Nothing in the package names an engine. Configuration reaches an engine as an opaque engine.Spec that the simulator hands over unread, so a second engine implements the interface in its own repository with no change here or in the simulator.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Does Add(r Request, now Time) error Hands over a request that arrived at now. Schedules nothing. Schedule(now Time) (Batch, error) Decides one batch: which requests run, how many tokens each, which are preempted, which KV transfers start. ErrNoCapacity when InFlightLimit batches are in flight. StepTime(b Batch) Duration Prices the forward pass of a batch that runs requests; at least one microsecond. An Empty batch is not priced. Complete(id BatchID, outcome Outcome, end Time) (Result, error) Applies a batch's outcome (tokens sampled, drafts accepted) and returns what became visible: tokens emitted, first tokens, finishes, KV events. TransferDone(id TransferID, ok bool, now Time) error Reports that an asynchronous KV load or store finished, successfully or not. Finish(id string, why FinishReason, now Time) error Ends a request for a reason the engine did not decide (client abort, timeout). A no-op for an unknown or finished request. NextWake(now Time) (Time, bool) The earliest instant after now at which state may change with no new input; false if none. InFlightLimit() int How many batches may be in flight at once (for vLLM, max_concurrent_batches); at least one. Metrics(now Time) Metrics The engine's exported metrics. Snapshot() State Current state (waiting, running, in-flight, KV capacity), a copy the caller may keep.

Calls are sequential: a simulator never calls an engine from two goroutines, and an engine starts none.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text: A batch that runs requests gets a BatchID greater than every earlier one of the same engine and stays in flight until Complete names it. Any number of batches may be in flight, up to InFlightLimit. They complete in the order they were scheduled (ErrOutOfOrder otherwise), which is how vLLM's engine core consumes its batch queue: it appends each scheduled batch at one end and takes results from the other. A batch that runs nothing (Empty) is not in flight, but may still start transfers.

docs.title: The wake protocol
docs.text:
• The simulator calls NextWake after every state-changing call (Add, Schedule, Complete, TransferDone, Finish, and a wake firing). An engine never cancels a wake: it reports a different instant, or false, the next time it is asked.
  • An earlier instant than the pending wake supersedes it; a later one, or false, replaces it.
  • The instant is always after now. A wake at or before now breaks the contract.
  • An engine with unfinished work, nothing in flight, no transfer outstanding and an empty Schedule must report a wake, or nothing would step it again.
  • At one instant a simulator processes, in this order: arrivals; transfer completions; batch completions; wakes and steps; timeouts last, so a request that completes at the instant its deadline passes has completed. An engine may rely on that order.

docs.title: Configuration: engine.Spec
docs.text:
Field Meaning Kind The engine model, such as vllm; the simulator looks it up in the factory registry. UpstreamVersion The real engine's release the configuration was written for. An engine refuses a release it does not model. Config The engine's configuration block, as YAML only the engine decodes. A factory decodes the node itself, so an error names its line in the document. Roots Directories the engine may read further inputs from, by role (catalog, registry, the configuration's own directory). Pool Which pool of a multi-pool document this engine is. Seed The run's seed.

engine.Register(f Factory) makes a factory available under its kind (it panics on an empty or a duplicate kind), engine.New(spec) builds an engine through it, and engine.Kinds() lists the registered kinds.

docs.title: Checking an implementation: engine/enginetest
docs.text: enginetest.Drive is a minimal discrete-event driver that follows the contract exactly. Driving an engine through it checks the laws every engine keeps, and reports the first one broken: no request is lost or finished twice, and none is finished that was never added; a batch runs only requests the engine holds, each once, and preempts only requests it holds and does not run, each once; batch IDs never repeat; batches complete in order; no more batches are in flight than the limit; a wake is always after the instant it was asked at; a step always takes time; a batch emits output only for its own requests, at most one sampled token plus its accepted drafts each; a finish reports the output tokens its batches emitted; an engine with work left always has a way to be stepped again; and the same inputs give the same run. enginetest.TestEngine runs those checks as a Go test, and enginetest.CheckProtocolErrors checks the error values. enginetest.FIFO is a deliberately simple engine built only through Spec and the registry: the proof that a second engine plugs in without changing this module.

docs.title: Rules: rules.EngineRules
docs.text: What one engine release accepts and refuses reaches a consumer, such as a cost model, through the rules.EngineRules interface rather than a concrete pack type, so the packs can live with the engine model that owns them. Rules packs lists the rules the registered packs check.

docs.title: Evaluation run
docs.text:
What a benchmark measured, one row per concurrency level, so that a prediction for the same scenario can be compared with it. The fields follow what benchmark harnesses already report.

For a validation case, use a measured run, which also records provenance, licence terms and metric definitions.

kind: EvaluationRun
name: llama-3.1-8b-on-h100-tp2-dp4
scenario: llama-3.1-8b-on-h100
harness: aiperf
engine_version: "0.29.0"
date: "2026-09-20"
points:
  - concurrency: 1
    completed_requests: 96
    output_tokens_per_sec: 157.3
    input_tokens_per_sec: 2543.0
    ttft_ms: 168.6
    itl_ms: 6.0
    mean_isl: 8015
    mean_osl: 496
    kv_utilization: 0.10
  - concurrency: 8
    completed_requests: 640
    output_tokens_per_sec: 1084.2
    ttft_ms: 212.4
    itl_ms: 7.1
    kv_utilization: 0.62
    prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.54

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always EvaluationRun. name string yes The run's identity. scenario string yes The scenario that was measured. harness string yes The benchmark harness that produced the numbers. Harnesses compute percentiles differently, so a comparison needs to know which. harness_version string no Its version. engine_version string yes The engine release the run exercised. It may differ from the scenario's. date string no When the measurement was taken, as an ISO 8601 date. points list yes At least one point, each at a different concurrency.

docs.title: points
docs.text:
Every field is as measured. Nothing is derived, so a reader can recompute any derived quantity and check it.

Key Type Required Meaning concurrency integer yes Simultaneous requests the harness kept in flight, at least 1. completed_requests integer no Requests finished at this level. output_tokens_per_sec number no Output throughput, tokens per second. input_tokens_per_sec number no Input throughput, tokens per second. ttft_ms number no Time to first token, ms. itl_ms number no Inter-token latency, ms. e2e_ms number no End-to-end latency, ms. mean_isl integer no Mean input length actually served. mean_osl integer no Mean output length actually served. kv_utilization number no Fraction of the KV pool in use, in [0, 1]. prefix_cache_hit_rate number no Fraction of prompt tokens served from cache, in [0, 1]. preemptions integer no Requests evicted and later recomputed. Nonzero means the engine ran out of KV cache space at this load.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A run is invalid if

  • kind is not EvaluationRun, or name, scenario, harness or engine_version is empty;
  • there are no points, a concurrency is below 1, or two points share a concurrency;
  • any number is not finite;
  • output_tokens_per_sec, ttft_ms or itl_ms is negative;
  • kv_utilization or prefix_cache_hit_rate lies outside [0, 1];
  • preemptions is negative.

A point with output throughput but neither ttft_ms nor itl_ms draws a warning: no prediction can be compared with it.

Source: spec/evaluation.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
Three schemas describe physical resources: a chip, an inter-node fabric, and the storage classes KV cache can be offloaded to. Every figure in them is a datasheet figure, or one computed from datasheet figures; Provenance says which. A measured correction to any of them is a coefficient and belongs in the registry.

The chip and fabric keys are in PascalCase, as the catalog's files write them. Each key carries its unit. All three schemas accept the catalog's _comment and _comment_* keys inside each chip, fabric and storage class, and discard them on load. Any other undeclared key, including any other key that begins with an underscore, is an error.

docs.title: Chip
docs.text:
A file under hardware/, named by its file.

hardware/h100.yaml
Provenance: vendor_spec
TFlopsPeak: 989.5
TFlopsFP8: 1979.0
BwPeakTBs: 3.35
MemoryGiB: 80.0
_comment_interconnect: "IntraNodeBwGBps is the on-package NVLink 4 link as a per-GPU NOMINAL unidirectional bandwidth in GB/s: 900 GB/s bidirectional datasheet spec => 450 unidirectional per GPU. vendor_spec (bidirectional / 2), NOT measured effective throughput; any measured correction is a per-cluster blis-registry number. The inter-node fabric figure and the intra:inter ratio it feeds (#1530) live with the reusable Network fabric class (networks/ib-400g.yaml), paired with this chip per deployment (a cluster/pool concept, #1662)."
IntraNodeBwGBps: 450
_comment_sm: "SMCount is the count of enabled Streaming Multiprocessors on the GH100 die as shipped in this part, from the NVIDIA datasheet (https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-tensor-core/nvidia-tensor-core-gpu-datasheet). H100 SXM5 enables 132 of the GH100 die's 144 SMs. The cost model uses SMCount for two things: the per-SM share of peak FLOPs, and the 12-SM derate a Triton-path KV fetch withholds while it overlaps a forward pass (cost model §8.3), which is 9.09% at 132 SMs and 11.11% at 108."
SMCount: 132
Key Type Required Meaning Provenance string yes Where the figures come from. One of the provenances. TFlopsPeak number yes Dense BF16 peak, TFLOP/s. TFlopsFP8 number no Dense FP8 peak, TFLOP/s. Omit on parts without native FP8. If set, it must exceed TFlopsPeak. TFlopsNVFP4 number no Dense NVFP4 (NVIDIA's 4-bit float) peak, TFLOP/s. Omit where the format is emulated rather than native. BwPeakTBs number yes HBM (on-package memory) bandwidth, TB/s. MemoryGiB number yes HBM capacity, GiB. IntraNodeBwGBps number yes On-node bandwidth per GPU, one direction, GB/s. NVLink where present. SMCount integer yes Streaming multiprocessors, positive. ComputeCapability string no CUDA compute capability, major.minor, such as 9.0 (H100, H200) or 10.0 (B200, GB200). A model graph that distinguishes architectures is resolved by the major version; one cannot be resolved for a chip that states none. GPUsPerNode integer no GPUs in one node. GPUsPerRack integer no GPUs in one rack, where a rack is a distinct link tier. A multiple of GPUsPerNode. IntraRackBwGBps number no Bandwidth between nodes inside a rack, GB/s. Needs GPUsPerRack.

docs.title: Fabric
docs.text:
A file under networks/, named by its file.

networks/ib-400g.yaml, comments omitted
Provenance: vendor_spec
InterNodeBwGBps: 50
Key Type Required Meaning Provenance string yes One of the provenances. InterNodeBwGBps number yes Bandwidth per GPU, one direction, GB/s: the NIC's line rate in Gb/s divided by eight. Nominal, not measured. RDMA boolean no Whether transfers bypass the CPU.

docs.title: Storage classes
docs.text:
One file, devices/storage.yaml, maps each storage class to its figures. The key is the class's name, which scenarios and deployments use. A name key inside a class is accepted and replaced by that key. Comment keys are allowed inside a class but not at the top level of the file, where every key is a class.

devices/storage.yaml
# Storage tiers for KV-cache offload.
# Split verbatim from the kv_offload_devices: section of the simulator's defaults.yaml.
nvme_gen4: {read_bandwidth_mb_s: 7.0e3, write_bandwidth_mb_s: 5.0e3, base_latency_us: 80.0}
nvme_gen3: {read_bandwidth_mb_s: 3.5e3, write_bandwidth_mb_s: 3.0e3, base_latency_us: 100.0}
sata_ssd:  {read_bandwidth_mb_s: 5.5e2, write_bandwidth_mb_s: 5.0e2, base_latency_us: 150.0}
cpu_dram:  {read_bandwidth_mb_s: 2.0e4, write_bandwidth_mb_s: 2.0e4, base_latency_us: 1.0}
s3:        {read_bandwidth_mb_s: 1.0e3, write_bandwidth_mb_s: 1.0e3, base_latency_us: 30000.0}
Key Type Required Meaning read_bandwidth_mb_s number yes Read bandwidth, MB/s. write_bandwidth_mb_s number yes Write bandwidth, MB/s. Separate because flash writes are slower than reads. base_latency_us number yes Fixed cost per transfer, µs. It dominates small transfers.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Every number must be finite. Beyond that, a chip is invalid if

  • Provenance is not recognized;
  • TFlopsPeak, BwPeakTBs, MemoryGiB or IntraNodeBwGBps is not positive;
  • SMCount is missing or not positive;
  • TFlopsFP8 or TFlopsNVFP4 is negative;
  • TFlopsFP8 is positive but not above TFlopsPeak; no shipped part has an FP8 peak at or below its BF16 peak, so this is almost always a transcription slip;
  • GPUsPerRack is not a multiple of GPUsPerNode, when both are set;
  • IntraRackBwGBps is set without GPUsPerRack;
  • ComputeCapability is set but is not major.minor.

A fabric is invalid if Provenance is not recognized or InterNodeBwGBps is not positive. A storage class is invalid if any of its three figures is not positive. devices/storage.yaml fails to load if it declares no class or a class with no value.

The catalog's convention that each SMCount cites a source in its _comment_sm prose is not checked, here or anywhere else, because comments are discarded before validation. Issue #32 records why it was left out of the schema.

docs.title: Why three schemas
docs.text:
A chip's peak rates belong to the die. A fabric belongs to the cluster: the same chip sits behind InfiniBand in one cluster and RoCE in another. Storage belongs to whoever provisioned the node. The cost of a collective that crosses nodes depends on the ratio of on-node to off-node bandwidth, which is a property of a chip paired with a fabric, not of either one. The ratio is therefore a function of both, hardware.IntraToInterRatio(chip, fabric), and not a key in either file.

Source: spec/hardware.

docs.title: Kernel interface
docs.text:
kernel.Kernel is the interface a cost model implements and a simulator calls. One value prices one pool of one deployment: how much memory a rank holds, how long a forward pass over a batch takes, and what transfers and host work cost. blis-latency-kernel is the implementation in use.

Every method is a pure function of its arguments and the configuration the kernel was constructed from: the same inputs give the same outputs, nothing is mutated, and calls are safe from several goroutines at once. There is no Init method; a kernel comes from its implementation's constructor, already resolved. Why the interface is drawn this way is the subject of Where the kernel stops.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Memory FixedBytes() MemoryBreakdown Per-rank memory that does not depend on the requests: weights, activation peak, captured CUDA graphs, redundant experts, communication buffers. SequenceFixedBytes() int64 Per-sequence memory that does not grow with length, such as recurrent state. Zero for a model with attention only. SequenceVariableBytes(tokens int) int64 Per-sequence memory for a given token count, quantized to the engine's page size. Step time StepTime(Batch) StepEstimate The time of one forward pass over a batch. Transfers TierTime(tier, dir, bytes, queueDepth) time.Duration One transfer to or from an offload tier. PDTransferTime(tokens, from, to Placement) time.Duration Moving one request's KV between pools. PDTransferDemand(tokens, from, to Placement) TransferDemand The same handoff as payload, floor and links, for a caller arbitrating concurrent transfers. Host work AdmissionOverhead(promptTokens int) time.Duration CPU work before a request can be scheduled, such as tokenization. Excludes queueing. OutputTokenOverhead() time.Duration Host work per emitted token, such as detokenization and streaming. CompletionOverhead() time.Duration Fixed work when a request finishes. Counts toward end-to-end latency, not time to first token. Provenance Provenance() []CoefficientOrigin Every coefficient the kernel used, with its set, method and scope. Resolved() Resolution What the kernel resolved, including requests it overrode. Deployment() deployment.Pool The pool it prices, as the document stated it.

Deployment() returns the request and Resolved() the resolution. For the parallel widths or the all-reduce backend, read Resolved(). For settings that resolution does not change, such as max_num_seqs and block_size, read the pool. The returned pool is a shallow copy; treat it as read-only.

docs.title: Step estimates
docs.text:
A step is priced as a sequence of stages, one per layer, since each layer needs the previous layer's output. Within a stage, work on different resources can overlap.

StepEstimate reports two bounds and a diagnosis:

Overlap Perfect overlap within each stage: the slowest resource in each stage, summed over the stages. NoOverlap No overlap anywhere: every resource's work, summed. Bottleneck The resource that did the most work over the step, which answers "what should be relieved". It is not the resource that set Overlap; since Overlap sums per-stage maxima, no single resource need account for it. PerResource Each resource's total, for a caller that needs to see why.

A configuration whose conclusion changes between the two bounds needs a measurement rather than a prediction.

The resources are:

sm · hbm · nvlink · nic · pcie · copy_engine · host

A collective appears under sm when the resolved backend is an SM-consuming kernel and under a link otherwise. The resolved backend decides this, not the requested one.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text:
A Batch is what the simulator supplies for one step.

Field Meaning Reqs []ReqShape One entry per request in the batch. DecodeThreshold int Engine configuration that selects the attention kernel for each request. SMBudget int SMs available this step: the chip's count less any held by a concurrent offload fetch. PadTokens int Tokens this data-parallel rank pads its step with under vLLM's DP lockstep: every rank runs the group's largest token count, and a rank with nothing scheduled runs a dummy batch of pad alone. Pad tokens run the GEMMs, the MoE dispatch and combine and the expert paths, but never the logits, the LM head, the vocabulary all-gather or sampling. They are not requests. 0 means none; never negative.

Each ReqShape carries the counts an engine's own scheduler reads:

Field Meaning Scheduled Tokens scheduled this step. Under speculative decoding a decoding request schedules the draft length plus one, so a count above 1 does not imply prefill. Computed Tokens already computed, as of batch formation. PromptLen The prompt length. With Computed, it tells the last chunk of a prefill split across steps apart from a decode. CachedTokens The prefix-cache hit, already subtracted from Scheduled. A count, not a rate.

Batch.Tokens() sums Scheduled, and Batch.PaddedTokens() adds PadTokens: the count the layers run. Batch.Validate() refuses a negative count. Batch.UniformDecode(width) reports whether every request schedules exactly width tokens. Some engine behavior, such as when dual-batch overlap engages, uses one threshold for such a batch and another for any other.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
A deployment states requests. The kernel's constructor decides what runs, and Resolution reports it.

Field Meaning TensorParallelWidth, DataParallelWidth, ExpertParallelWidth The resolved layout. The expert width is tp × pcp × dp with expert parallelism on, and 1 with it off. AllReduceBackend The all-reduce that will run, which may differ from the request. AsyncScheduling The resolved value of the tri-state request. CascadeAttention Whether cascade attention is available after every condition is applied. SequenceParallelMoE Whether the MoE input is made sequence-parallel, replacing an all-reduce with a reduce-scatter and all-gather. Overrides []Override Each request the layout could not honor: the field, what was requested, what was resolved, and why.

A width of zero means unset, not "no parallelism". TensorParallel(), DataParallel() and ExpertParallel() return the widths with a floor of one, for a reader that may see a zero value.

docs.title: Transfer demand
docs.text:
PDTransferTime prices a handoff as if it ran alone. A simulator running several at once needs to know which links they share, and which part of each price sharing stretches. PDTransferDemand answers both:

Field Meaning Bytes int64 The payload. Floor time.Duration Time the transfer takes however much bandwidth it gets. Sharing a link does not lengthen it. Links []LinkUse Every link the payload crosses, each named once: a LinkID and the rate the link offers to a transfer alone on it.

A LinkID is opaque. Two demands naming the same ID share that link while both are in flight, and IDs are comparable across the kernels of one deployment.

The law is part of the contract: alone, a demand costs exactly what PDTransferTime charges, max(Floor, Bytes / slowest link rate), or Floor with no links. TransferDemand.AloneTime() is that definition, including its conversion to a duration, so an implementation that computes PDTransferTime from its own demand satisfies the law by construction.

The kernel states the links; it never sees other transfers. How a shared link's bandwidth is divided is the simulator's to decide, and the schema does not prescribe it.

Package kernel/kerneltest checks the law against any implementation, the way testing/fstest checks a file system:

func TestPDTransferLaw(t *testing.T) {
    k := newKernel(t) // the implementation under test
    kerneltest.TestPDTransfer(t, k, kerneltest.PDCases())
}

PDCases covers a same-node, a same-rack and a cross-rack handoff at token counts from 0 to 131,072. CheckPDTransfer checks one case and returns an error, for a caller with cases of its own; TestPDTransfer fails when given no cases, since it would then check nothing. CheckLinksAgree checks that two kernels of one deployment name the same links at the same rates for one handoff, and that both demands are well formed. CheckPDTransfer requires a well-formed demand (TransferDemand.Check, which also refuses a payload that crosses no link, since an arbiter would then have nothing to share), the same demand from two calls, and an exact match with PDTransferTime. TestPDTransfer also requires that more tokens never move fewer bytes between one pair of placements; it does not require the floor to stay fixed, since per-transfer overhead can grow with the pages a transfer moves.

Adding a method to Kernel breaks every other implementation, fakes included, until it adds the method.

docs.title: Other types
docs.text:
Type Meaning MemoryBreakdown Weights, ActivationPeak, CUDAGraph, EPLBRedundant, CommBuffers, in bytes; Total() sums them. Direction to_tier (eviction) or from_tier (fetch). Priced separately because flash reads and writes differ. Placement A rank's Node, Rack and Pool (the pool's role). Comparing two placements chooses the link a transfer uses. CoefficientOrigin One row of the provenance trail: entry Name, Set, Method, Scope.

Source: kernel.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes Always MeasuredRun. name string yes The run's identity, a lowercase slug. In the catalog, also its file name. schema_version integer yes Always 1. source mapping yes Where the numbers came from, below. model string no The catalog model that was served. engine_version string no The engine release that ran. cluster mapping no The cluster it ran on. Coefficients are not part of a measurement, so this is the cluster alone. deployment mapping no The deployment that ran, checked against cluster when both are present. router mapping no The router in front of the deployment, below. workload mapping no The workload binding that reproduces the request stream. client mapping yes The load generator, below. metric_defs mapping yes Each metric's definition, keyed by metric name. points list yes One entry per load level, strictly increasing. The first is the anchor shape error is measured from. provenance list no One row per setting, comparing the sources that state it. diff list no Each difference between the measured configuration and BLIS's. verdict string no EXACT, PARTIAL or NOT_REPRODUCIBLE. If present, must equal the computed verdict. resolution string with EXACT STRICT or RESOLVED. If present, must equal the computed resolution. duplicate_of string no Another run with the same model, hardware, loads and values. supersedes string no A run this one replaces.

docs.title: source
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes The publisher. One of the source kinds. adapter mapping yes The extracting code: name, version and the sha256 of its source. inputs list yes Every file read, each with its digest. At least one has role report. extraction mapping yes How values were read, below. retrieved_utc string no When the inputs were fetched, RFC 3339 in UTC. license_ref string yes The entry in measurements/sources.yaml whose terms govern the run. Key Type Required Meaning name string yes The adapter's path or name. version string yes Its version. sha256 string yes Digest of its source, 64 lowercase hex characters. Key Type Required Meaning role string yes What the file is to the run. One of the input roles. url string url or path Where it was fetched from, http(s). repo string no The repository holding it. commit string no The commit it was read at. path string url or path Its path in the repository or the local store. git_blob string no Its git blob id. size integer no Its size in bytes. sha256 string yes Its digest, 64 lowercase hex characters. fetched_utc string no When it was fetched, RFC 3339 in UTC. note string no Anything a reader needs, such as how an excerpt was cut. Every method parses; none executes downloaded content. selectors list no What was read: literal names, columns, row ids. label_verified boolean no Whether each metric label was checked against the harness's definition.

docs.title: client
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning harness string no The load generator. A run without one cannot be EXACT. harness_version string no Its version. image_digest string no The client image, pinned by sha256:<64 hex>. command list no The argv as recorded. seed integer no The client seed. 0 is a seed. num_prompts integer no Requests per level. Not negative. burstiness number no Gamma shape of the arrivals; 1 is Poisson. Positive. ramp_up mapping no A rate ramp: strategy (linear or exponential), start, end. num_warmups integer no Warmup requests, excluded from the metrics. ignore_eos boolean no Whether output ran to max_tokens regardless of EOS. endpoint string no The API endpoint, such as completions or chat. tokenizer mapping no The tokenizer the client counted with: repo (required), revision, sha256, mode. duration_s number no Measurement duration per level, seconds. grace_s number no Grace period after the duration, seconds. Key Type Required Meaning strategy string yes linear or exponential. start number yes Starting rate, requests per second. end number yes Final rate, requests per second. Key Type Required Meaning repo string yes The tokenizer's repository. revision string no The revision it was read at. sha256 string no Digest of the tokenizer files. mode string no The tokenizer mode, when the engine selects among several.

docs.title: metric_defs
docs.text:
Each definition is keyed by the metric name the points use. A field left out is unstated, and any unstated formula, population, clock, or statistic (denominator for a throughput) keeps the run from EXACT: a scorer cannot tell whether a BLIS metric is the same quantity.

Key Type Required Meaning formula string no The quantity, such as ttft or output_throughput. statistic string no mean, median, std, max, or a percentile pNN. Not for a throughput. population string no What the statistic is over: per_request, pooled_chunks or pooled_tokens. denominator string no What a throughput divides by. Only for a throughput. clock string no client or server timestamps; simulated only in a Result. start_event string no When a latency starts. stop_event string no When a latency stops. output_len_source string no Where output token counts come from. reasoning_counted_as_content boolean no Whether reasoning tokens count as output. percentile_method string with a percentile How a percentile interpolates; numpy_linear. unit string yes ms, tokens_per_s or requests_per_s; must be the formula's. cite string yes Where the definition is read from: a harness file and line, or the report's text.

docs.title: points
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning id string yes Unique within the run. load mapping yes concurrency, request_rate, or both. Every point uses the same ones. metrics mapping yes Measured values keyed by a name in metric_defs, each value finite and not negative. completed integer no Requests completed. failed integer no Requests failed. realized mapping no mean_isl and mean_osl actually served. kv_utilization number no Fraction of the KV pool in use, in [0, 1]. prefix_hit_rate number no Fraction of prompt tokens served from cache, in [0, 1]. preemptions integer no Requests evicted and recomputed. noise mapping no Run-to-run spread: seeds (at least 2) and cv. Key Type Required Meaning concurrency integer concurrency or request_rate The client's concurrency cap. request_rate number concurrency or request_rate Offered requests per second. An unbounded rate under a cap is the cap alone. Key Type Required Meaning value number yes The measured value, in the definition's unit. report_label string no The label the report gave it. raw_key string no The key, column or row it was read from. label_verified boolean no Whether the label was checked against the definition. Key Type Required Meaning mean_isl number no Mean input length served. mean_osl number no Mean output length served. Key Type Required Meaning seeds integer yes Seeds the spread was measured over, at least 2. cv number yes Coefficient of variation across them.

docs.title: provenance
docs.text:
One row per setting, comparing the report, the script that produced it, the run's own artifact, and the value BLIS would use.

Key Type Required Meaning setting string yes The setting, unique within the run. report mapping no The report's value. script mapping no The producing script's value. artifact mapping no The run artifact's value. blis mapping no The value BLIS uses. verdict string yes MATCH or MISMATCH (at least two values listed), UNSTATED (at most one of report, script, artifact), or UNVERIFIABLE (report and script, no artifact). resolved_by string no For UNSTATED only: the engine rule, at the pinned version, that fixes the value. material string yes yes, no, unknown, or bounded. bound string with bounded How far it can move a metric. note string no Anything a reader needs. Key Type Required Meaning value string yes The value as that source states it. ref string except under blis Where the source states it. commit string no The commit the source was read at.

docs.title: diff
docs.text: Key Type Required Meaning path string yes The field that differs. measured string no The measured value. blis string no The value BLIS uses. kind string yes not_expressible, not_modelled, conflict, unresolved, or approximated. removable boolean no Whether a change in owner_repo would close it. owner_repo string when removable The repository that owns the change. material string yes yes, no, unknown, or bounded. bound string with bounded How far it can move a metric. issue string no The issue tracking it.

docs.title: router
docs.text:
The router is described by kind; an endpoint picker is pinned by the digest of its config, whose bytes the simulator reads.

Key Type Required Meaning kind string yes direct or epp. epp mapping with epp The picker. Not allowed with direct. Key Type Required Meaning version string yes The picker's version. image string no Its image. config mapping yes Its plugin config: path and sha256. flow_control string no A summary of the flow-control settings. Key Type Required Meaning path string yes The config file. sha256 string yes Its digest, 64 lowercase hex characters.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
The verdict is computed; a stated one must match.

NOT_REPRODUCIBLE BLIS cannot build the run: model, engine_version, cluster, deployment or workload is missing, or a diff entry is not_expressible. EXACT Otherwise, when the diff is empty, no provenance row is MISMATCH or UNVERIFIABLE, every UNSTATED row has resolved_by, every metric definition is complete, the client harness is recorded, and the licence permits scoring. Resolution is RESOLVED when a row was resolved by a rule and STRICT otherwise. Only an EXACT run may anchor calibration. PARTIAL Any other run. It is scored and reported apart from EXACT runs.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
A run is invalid if

  • kind is not MeasuredRun, name is not a lowercase slug, or schema_version is not 1;
  • a vocabulary value is not recognized, or a digest is not 64 lowercase hex characters;
  • the source has no adapter name, version or digest, no inputs, no report input, or an input without a url or path;
  • a timestamp is not RFC 3339 UTC, or the client image is not pinned by digest;
  • the cluster, deployment, router or workload is invalid, or the deployment does not fit the cluster;
  • a metric definition has no unit or cite, a unit that is not its formula's, a statistic on a throughput, a denominator on a latency, or a percentile without a method;
  • there are no points, two share an id, a point states no load, points mix load modes or are not strictly increasing, or a metric has no definition or a negative or non-finite value;
  • a provenance row's sources do not support its verdict, resolved_by is on a row that is not UNSTATED, or bound is missing for bounded or present otherwise;
  • a removable difference names no owner_repo;
  • a string carries a credential: a token, a private key, a Kubernetes Secret reference, or a kubeconfig path;
  • a stated verdict or resolution is not the computed one.
